purpose: Consolidated human labels and script diagnoses for skeleton QC threshold and ablation design.

label_taxonomy.acceptable_flagged: Human-reviewed segment that looks acceptable even though the temporal skeleton check flagged it.
label_taxonomy.review: Candidate segment requiring another human pass.
label_taxonomy.algorithm_outcome_true_positive: The temporal skeleton check broadly caught the human-confirmed abnormal segment.
label_taxonomy.algorithm_outcome_partial: The temporal skeleton check caught only part of the human-confirmed abnormal segment.
label_taxonomy.algorithm_outcome_false_negative: The human-confirmed abnormal segment was mostly missed by temporal geometry.
label_taxonomy.algorithm_outcome_false_positive: The temporal skeleton check flagged a visually acceptable segment.

rule_development_notes.name: mask_containment_needed
rule_development_notes.description: Temporal geometry misses cases where keypoints are visibly detached from the hand but remain temporally stable or only jump briefly.

rule_development_notes.name: temporal_gap_closing
rule_development_notes.description: A short gap inside a strong abnormal segment should be bridged before segment-level reporting.

rule_development_notes.name: fast_motion_false_positive_control
rule_development_notes.description: Borderline or acceptable fast motion can trigger current single-frame thresholds, especially rotation_delta and displacement.

rule_development_notes.name: rotation_only_false_positive_control
rule_development_notes.description: Fine dishwashing motions can trigger rotation_delta-only or rotation-plus-angle flags while acceleration and displacement remain low. These should probably be downgraded unless supported by containment or additional motion signals.

rule_development_notes.name: rotation_as_review_route
rule_development_notes.description: Large or sustained rotation changes should not always be a hard temporal failure by themselves, but they are useful as a route into SAM3/mask containment review when the hand may leave frame or keypoints rotate incorrectly.

rule_development_notes.name: keypoint_presence_gate
rule_development_notes.description: If the supplier HDF5 exposes missing per-joint validity, NaN coordinates, or fewer than 21 usable points, that frame should be assigned zero/rejected before SAM3. If HDF5 only stores 21 numeric points without visibility, this cannot be reliably inferred from geometry alone.

rule_development_notes.name: fine_manipulation_visual_failure
rule_development_notes.description: Dishwashing or other fine manipulation can produce visually poor keypoint following without large temporal jitter on most frames. This probably cannot be solved by simply lowering temporal thresholds without increasing false positives.

candidate_ablation_rules.name: relaxed_thresholds
candidate_ablation_rules.description: Less sensitive thresholds for fast folding motions.

candidate_ablation_rules.name: temporal_persistence
candidate_ablation_rules.description: Require at least 3 consecutive flagged frames before a hard suspect segment.

candidate_ablation_rules.name: short_gap_closing
candidate_ablation_rules.description: Bridge 1-2 unflagged frames between two flagged runs when surrounding frames are strongly abnormal.

candidate_ablation_rules.name: multi_signal
candidate_ablation_rules.description: Require at least two metrics to exceed thresholds on the same frame for high-confidence temporal flags.

candidate_ablation_rules.name: mask_containment
candidate_ablation_rules.description: Add image/mask containment to catch stable wrong keypoints and hand-out-of-view cases.
